name: asdf-canonical
instr:
Restore the documented behavior of the ASDF library in this repository.

The subsystem in scope is the `asdf` Python package's own modules and subpackages, excluding the vendored trees `asdf/_jsonschema/` and `asdf/_extern/` and the test support under `asdf/_tests/`, `asdf/testing/` and `asdf/conftest.py`, together with the documentation under `docs/` and the top-level `README.rst` and `CITATION.rst`.

The docstrings, attribute comments and doctests those modules carry are part of that documentation.

That documentation is the authority. Read it, compare every behavioral contract it states against the implementation, and restore all behavior affected by the drift.

Nothing here tells you which files, functions or behaviors the drift touches, or how many there are; determining that from the documentation is the task. Preserve public APIs and behavior outside this subsystem, and keep the documentation as it stands. Work offline.

Before you edit any code, write your research and your plan to /workdir/RESEARCH_AND_PLANNING.md. Cover what you learned about the existing code and the constraints that shape the change, then how you intend to carry it out and why, including how you will know it works. Be concrete — the files, names and decisions specific to this codebase, not generalities. Complete the document before you touch any code: it is the record of your up-front investigation and decisions, and it should not be rewritten to match whatever the implementation turns into afterw
